7730-paul-clifford-volume-03.title: Paul Clifford Volume 03
7730-paul-clifford-volume-03.creator: Edward Bulwer-Lytton
7730-paul-clifford-volume-03.description: A book by Edward Bulwer-Lytton. "'Sdeath, Ned!" said his comrade, who had for some time been plunged in a silent revery,--"'Sdeath! why can you not stifle your love for the fine arts at a moment like this? That hum of thine grows louder every moment; at last I expect it will burst out into a full roar. Recollect we are not at Gentleman George's now!"

arxiv-2010-12395.title: Local dendritic balance enables learning of efficient representations in networks of spiking neurons
arxiv-2010-12395.creator: Fabian A. Mikulasch
arxiv-2010-12395.description: Abstract Abstract How can neural networks learn to efficiently represent complex and high-dimensional inputs via local plasticity mechanisms? Classical models of representation learning assume that input weights are learned via pairwise Hebbian-like plasticity. Here, we show that pairwise Hebbian-like plasticity only works under unrealistic requirements on neural dynamics and input statistics.

arxiv-2102-05544.title: Central limit theorem for lozenge tilings with curved limit shape
arxiv-2102-05544.creator: Benoît Laslier
arxiv-2102-05544.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Benoît Laslier. It has been well known for a long time that the height function of random lozenge tilings of large domains follow a law of large number and possible limits called dimer limit shapes are well understood. For the next order, it is expected that fluctuations behave like version of a Gaussian Free field, at least away from some special “frozen” regions. However despite being one of the main questions in the domain for 20 years, only special cases have been obtained.

arxiv-2106-02105.title: A Little Robustness Goes a Long Way: Leveraging Robust Features for Targeted Transfer Attacks
arxiv-2106-02105.creator: Jacob M. Springer, Melanie Mitchell, Garrett T. Kenyon
arxiv-2106-02105.description: Abstract Adversarial examples for neural network image classifiers are known to be transferable: examples optimized to be misclassified by a source classifier are often misclassified as well by classifiers with different architectures. However, targeted adversarial examples—optimized to be classified as a chosen target class—tend to be less transferable between architectures.

arxiv-2205-02624.title: Correspondence Theory for Generalized Modal Algebras
arxiv-2205-02624.creator: Zhiguang Zhao
arxiv-2205-02624.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Zhiguang Zhao. In the present paper, we give a systematic study of the correspondence theory of generalized modal algebras and generalized modal spaces, in the spirit of [ 3 , 6 ] . The special feature of the present paper is that in the proof of the (right-handed) topological Ackermann lemma, the admissible valuations are not the clopen valuations anymore, but values in the set 𝒟 𝒦 ​ ( X ) \mathcal{D}_{\mathcal{K}}(X) which are only closed and satisfy additional properties, not necessarily open.

arxiv-2512-21273.title: Operational Calculus for the n n th-Level Prabhakar Type Fractional Derivative with Applications
arxiv-2512-21273.creator: Imtiaz Waheed 1,2 , Erkinjon Karimov 1 , Mujeeb ur Rehman 2
arxiv-2512-21273.description: Abstract . This study investigates the n th-level Prabhakar fractional derivative, a generalization encompassing some well-known fractional derivatives. We establish its fundamental properties, particularly its relationship with the corresponding Prabhakar fractional integral. Furthermore, we develop Mikusiński-type operational calculus for this derivative, providing a framework for solving differential equations involving this operator.

pmc-11446190.title: Understanding the Support Needs and Challenges Faced by Family Caregivers in the Care of Their Older Adults at Home [Letter]
pmc-11446190.creator: Zhanshuo Xiao, Yilin Jiang, Narina A Samah
pmc-11446190.description: ng conflict in the Tigray region. It identifies key challenges such as financial strain, inadequate communication with healthcare providers, medication management difficulties, and transportation barriers—issues that are further intensified by the conflict. The use of a phenomenological approach to explore these lived experiences is effective, providing a comprehensive understanding of the intricate realities faced by family caregivers.

pmc-11689654.title: Predictive model using autism diagnostic observation schedule, second edition for differential diagnosis between schizophrenia and autism spectrum disorder
pmc-11689654.creator: Dan Nakamura, Yoichi Hanawa, Shizuka Seki, Misato Yamauchi, Yuriko Iwami, Yuta Nagatsuka, Hirohisa Suzuki, Keisuke Aoyagi, Wakaho Hayashi, Takeshi Otowa, Akira Iwanami
pmc-11689654.description: BackgroundAlthough schizophrenia and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) are currently conceptualized as distinct disorders, the similarity in their symptoms often makes differential diagnosis difficult. This study aimed to identify similarities and differences in the symptoms of schizophrenia and ASD to establish a more useful and objective differential diagnostic method and to identify ASD traits in participants with schizophrenia.

pmc-12366514.title: Qualitative study on the sense of meaning in life in uremic patients undergoing initial hemodialysis
pmc-12366514.creator: Chenyang Li, Yan Shan, Xiangdong Yan, Zihao Wang
pmc-12366514.description: BackgroundFor patients with uraemia, the most effective treatment, aside from surgical interventions like kidney transplantation, is maintenance haemodialysis. First-time haemodialysis patients often lack an understanding of the treatment, making them susceptible to negative emotions such as anxiety and depression, as well as shifts in their perception of life’s meaning.

pmc-12578771.title: Correlation Between Infectivity and qRT-PCR Values for Murine Norovirus Recovered from Frozen Berries
pmc-12578771.creator: Daniel Plante, Julio Alexander Bran Barrera, Maude Lord, Jennifer Harlow, Irène Iugovaz, Neda Nasheri
pmc-12578771.description: Human norovirus (HuNoV) is the leading cause of acute gastroenteritis globally, with frozen berries frequently implicated in foodborne outbreaks. Current surveillance relies on quantitative reverse transcription PCR (qRT-PCR), which cannot differentiate between infectious and non-infectious viral particles, complicating risk assessment.

pmc-12586631.title: The emerging landscape of brain glycosylation: from molecular complexity to therapeutic potential
pmc-12586631.creator: Youngsuk Seo, Ji Eun Park, Jae Young Yu, Boyoung Lee, Jong Hyuk Yoon, Hyun Joo An
pmc-12586631.description: Glycosylation functions as a pivotal posttranslational modification in proteins and as a distinct biosynthetic process in lipids. In the brain, it plays essential roles in development, function and homeostasis by modulating protein folding, receptor trafficking and intercellular communication. Although glycans constitute less than 1% of the brain’s mass, their impact is disproportionately profound.

pmc-12611850.title: Case Report: Head injury presenting as lower cranial nerve palsy
pmc-12611850.creator: Shubham Gupta, Rakesh Gupta, Zafar Sheikh, Abhijeet Bele
pmc-12611850.description: Lower cranial nerve palsy is a rare condition, most commonly caused by malignant skull base lesions or internal carotid artery dissection, and only rarely resulting from trauma. We report two cases of road traffic accident victims presenting with lower cranial nerve palsy involving cranial nerves IX, X, and XI. Both patients had similar clinical complaints.

pmc-12717873.title: Chrono-Immune Neuropathy During PD-1 Blockade: A Report of a Fatal Case and Hypothesis on Circadian Modulation of Neurotoxicity
pmc-12717873.creator: Ivan Bivolarski
pmc-12717873.description: Immune checkpoint inhibitors can cause a wide spectrum of immune-related adverse events, including rare but severe neurological complications. This report describes a fatal case of progressive immune-mediated neuropathy in a melanoma patient treated with PD-1 blockade, in whom worsening neuropathic pain and functional decline coincided with irregular, non-aligned timing of immunotherapy infusions.

pmc-13056900.title: Explainable LSTM-AdamW based fault diagnosis of aircraft rotating components using airborne acoustic signals under dynamic operating conditions
pmc-13056900.creator: Yıldırım Özüpak, Emrah Aslan, Ievgen Zaitsev
pmc-13056900.description: Acoustic signal (AS) has emerged as a powerful non-contact technique for early detection of incipient faults in aircraft rotating components due to its high sensitivity to transient damage mechanisms. However, the strong non-stationarity and noise susceptibility of acoustic signals under dynamically varying operating conditions present significant challenges for reliable fault diagnosis.

pmc-13078953.title: Research on Quantitative Analysis Technology for Pacific White Shrimp Density Based on Environmental DNA
pmc-13078953.creator: Guangyan Liang, Sizhe Wang, Shan Wang, Yusheng Jiang, Yuxue Qin
pmc-13078953.description: Litopenaeus vannamei is one of the most essential farmed shrimp species globally, yet disease outbreaks during cultivation continue to hinder industry development. Accurate biomass estimation is critical for optimizing feeding, maintaining water quality, and preventing disease. This study developed a quantitative method for environmental DNA (eDNA) using real‐time fluorescence quantitative PCR with L. vannamei as the model species.

pmc-13091224.title: Primary care diagnosed multimorbidity and risk of venous thromboembolism in Sweden
pmc-13091224.creator: Jonatan Ahrén, MirNabi Pirouzifard, Björn Holmquist, Jan Sundquist, Kristina Sundquist, Bengt Zöller
pmc-13091224.description: BackgroundMultimorbidity, the co-occurrence of two or more non-communicable diseases (NCDs), is common and has been linked to venous thromboembolism (VTE). Whether multimorbidity diagnosed in primary-care is associated with incident VTE remains unclear. We aimed to examine this association.MethodsMultimorbidity was defined using Swedish primary-care data.

pmc-13348425.title: All-inside Circumferential Fiber Augmentation of Medial Meniscus Combined with Medial Open-wedge High Tibial Osteotomy
pmc-13348425.creator: Woon-Hwa Jung, Abbas Bhatia, Rahul Singh, Dong-Hyun Kim
pmc-13348425.description: Introduction:Medial meniscus posterior root tears (MMPRTs) in varus knees accelerate medial compartment degeneration. While medial open-wedge high tibial osteotomy (MOWHTO) reduces compartmental load, it does not restore meniscal hoop tension. Circumferential fiber augmentation (CFA) may improve meniscal stability and limit extrusion.Case Report:A 49-year-old female with varus alignment and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-confirmed MMPRT underwent single-stage all-inside CFA followed by MOWHTO.

pmc-13674344.title: The effects of pH on cortex and condensate formation
pmc-13674344.creator: Brooke E Waechtler, Chujun Liu, Bethany A Todd, Oiza Dimowo, Emma P Morin, Jasmine Barraza, Mashal Nawabi, Constance Campbell, Douglas N Robinson
pmc-13674344.description: Waechtler et al. discover that a pH differential between the actin cortical and cytoplasmic phases of the cell serves as one mechanism that controls actin cytoskeletal reorganization. Specifically, a pH gradient between these two phases may mediate the transition between cortex construction beneath the membrane and cytoskeletal protein condensate formation throughout the cytoplasm.
